body:
## Affected component

CWS project-feedback issue routing. Feedback about CWS-owned commands has been filed in the Hieronymus tracker.

## Minimal reproduction / observed evidence

Hieronymus issue #53 reported missing layout-aware journaled relocation in `cw layout` / migration tooling (CWS 0.10.1, cw 0.2.0), and stated that it was reported there according to feedback-routing instructions. The failed component belongs to CWS. The maintainer has now transferred it to https://github.com/InkyQuill/creative-writing-skills/issues/16.

Original location: https://github.com/InkyQuill/hieronymus/issues/53 (redirects after transfer).

This is an observed misrouting, not a deterministic reproduction of the agent's routing decision.

## Expected behavior

Choose the tracker from the failed component, even when the writing project uses Hieronymus. CWS CLI/layout/migration/skills and CWS integration wrappers belong here; Hieronymus service, hiero CLI, MCP and its own skills belong in Hieronymus.

## Actual behavior

A CWS CLI defect reached Hieronymus instead. The current canonical `cw/skills/project-feedback/SKILL.md` and installed CWS 0.10.1 instructions already describe the correct ownership rule, so an incorrect URL in that file is not established as the cause.

## Requested fix

Audit the effective routing path, including integration instructions and generated/distributed skills, for competing tracker defaults. Add a regression scenario: a CWS layout/migration defect inside a Hieronymus-enabled literary project must select the CWS tracker; an actual Hieronymus service defect must select Hieronymus. Record the actual source of the conflicting routing once reproduced.

## Impact / environment

Wrong tracker ownership obscures the backlog and requires manual transfers. Evidence contains only public issue metadata; no manuscript, credentials or private prompt text.
title: CWS feedback issues are filed in Hieronymus despite component ownership

CWS 0.10.1 / cw 0.2.0 supports custom root-level folders via `cw layout`, but offers no journaled relocation command for an existing canonical authoring project. `edit apply` cannot move files. Migration validation calls `allowed_document_kind(destination)` without project layout and rejects noncanonical destinations and non-Markdown assets; migration also scaffolds the legacy tree.

Use case: flatten `work/drafts` to a chosen root folder and `kb/characters` to `characters`, preserving working status, images, Pocket Editor binders/sidecars and updating references.

Please provide a preview/apply relocation operation honoring layout roles, exact-byte opaque files, relative links, draft targets, generated indexes and undo. Current workaround requires a one-off adapter to the bundled transaction engine. Reported here per project feedback-routing instructions.
title: CWS: no layout-aware journaled relocation for existing canonical projects

body:
## Documentation gap

`cw edit replace` matches only the Markdown **body** of a document, not its frontmatter. The command reference recommends putting large anchors and replacement bodies in files, but does not say that `--old-file` containing the whole physical file (including YAML frontmatter) will always report zero matches.

## Reproduction

With CWS `cw 0.2.0`, copy a KB page with frontmatter to `/tmp/old.md` and verify `cmp -s kb/styles/system-windows.md /tmp/old.md` succeeds. Then run:

```sh
python3 <installed-project-maintenance>/resources/cli/cw.py edit replace kb/styles/system-windows.md --old-file /tmp/old.md --new-file /tmp/new.md --expect-count 1 --format json
```

Observed: `expected 1 match(es), found 0`. A body-only anchor works. An anchor solely in the YAML frontmatter also reports zero. Source inspection shows `_plan_text_edit` deliberately searches `document.body`, so the matching behavior is intentional.

Expected documentation/diagnostic: state in `cw edit replace` help and the command reference that anchors must be taken from the body; point users to `frontmatter-set` for metadata edits. A more specific conflict message for an anchor that exists only in frontmatter would also help. This confused a previewed KB update because byte-identical source files appeared not to match.

comments.body: Документация и справка команды обновлены в #11: текстовые якоря ищутся только в Markdown body, без YAML frontmatter; для обычных метаданных указан frontmatter-set в edit apply. Сообщение о конфликте пакетного редактирования теперь включает операцию и путь.

title: Document that cw edit replace anchors match Markdown body only

body:
## Summary

`cw edit apply` reports `expected 1 match(es), found 0` when one transaction contains two `replace` operations with the same `old` string for two different files, even though each operation has its own distinct `path`. Removing those two operations lets the remaining transaction preview normally.

## Reproduction

Use an operations array like:

```json
[
  {
    "op": "replace",
    "path": "kb/characters/antoine.md",
    "old": "  - \"same source\"",
    "new": "  - \"updated source\""
  },
  {
    "op": "replace",
    "path": "kb/characters/supporting.md",
    "old": "  - \"same source\"",
    "new": "  - \"updated source\""
  }
]
```

Both source files contain exactly one matching line. Preview with `cw edit apply operations.json --format json`.

## Actual

The whole preview aborts with:

```json
{"exit_status": 1, "message": "expected 1 match(es), found 0", "status": "conflict"}
```

No failing operation or path is reported.

## Expected

Matching should be scoped to each operation's `path`, so both replacements preview successfully. If one operation does fail, the error should identify its operation index and path.

Observed with creative-writing-skills 0.9.0 on 2026-09-20.

comments.body: В #11 закреплён тест с двумя replace-операциями с одинаковым old для разных файлов: обе операции успешно планируются. Исходный конфликт с найденными 0 совпадений на текущем коде не воспроизвёлся. Если отдельная операция действительно не совпадает, сообщение теперь показывает её номер и path, чтобы можно было диагностировать конкретный файл. При новом воспроизведении с этими данными issue можно открыть повторно.

title: cw edit apply conflicts on identical old text in different paths

body:
## Проблема

Команда cw edit replace читает old-file с обязательным завершающим переводом строки. Для replace используется flexible_whitespace, поэтому этот перевод строки становится пробельным фрагментом регулярного выражения и может поглотить не только конец строки якоря, но и пустую строку после него в целевом Markdown.

В результате точечная замена абзаца удаляет пустую строку перед следующим заголовком или абзацем. Предпросмотр показывает постороннее изменение форматирования.

## Воспроизведение

1. В Markdown есть абзац, пустая строка и следующий заголовок.
2. old-file содержит только заменяемый абзац; обычный текстовый файл заканчивается переводом строки.
3. Запустить cw edit replace с old-file и new-file.
4. В diff пустая строка после вставленного текста исчезает.

## Обходной путь

Использовать cw edit apply с JSON-операцией, где строки old и new не оканчиваются переводом строки.

## Ожидание

Завершающий перевод строки old-file не должен расширять совпадение на последующий структурный пробел Markdown либо файловый интерфейс должен явно сохранять границу якоря. Предпросмотр не должен удалять соседние пробельные разделители, которых нет в смысловом якоре.

comments.body: Исправлено в #11: завершающий перевод строки в якоре замены больше не поглощает следующую пустую строку Markdown. Добавлены регрессионные тесты для обычной строки и строки с горизонтальными пробелами перед переводом.

title: CWS: cw edit replace съедает пробельный разделитель после якоря из файла

body:
### Контекст

`cw check all` прогоняет прозаический линтинг (как минимум CW-PROSE-103 — неразрывные пробелы после однобуквенных слов) по всем главам, включая рабочие черновики `work/drafts/`. В нашем проекте черновики глав 1–15 дали ~630 предупреждений типографики, хотя главы 1–5 были нормализованы ранее.

### Проблема

- Черновик по определению многократно правится: выравнивать типографику в нём вручную — работа, которая повторяется и шумит в отчётах `check all`.
- Ручной построчный фикс (десятки replace-операций в транзакции) — механическая нагрузка на агента, не создающая ценности для истории.
- Линтинг имеет смысл там, где текст становится результатом: при приёме черновика в `story/chapters/` (или `story/side-stories/`).

### Предложение

1. **Прозаический линтинг применять только к результирующим главам** (`story/chapters/`, `story/side-stories/`) — для черновиков `work/drafts/` проверки вида CW-PROSE-103 не предупреждать (или выносить в отдельную opt-in команду вида `cw check prose-drafts`).
2. **Автоматизация вместо ручной правки:** для типографских правил, которые допускают механический фикс (неразрывные пробелы после однобуквенных слов, NBSP перед срединными тире), — команда автоприменения, например `cw fix --prose-typography <path>`, чтобы нормализация запускалась одной командой (естественное место — шаг приёма главы, draft → accepted), а не построчными правками.

### Пример из проекта

- Черновики глав 6–15: ~60–75 предупреждений CW-PROSE-103 на главу при том, что проза устраивает автора; нормализация не меняет ни одного слова прозы.
- Ручной фикс занял несколько транзакций построчных замен — ровно та работа, которую просит автоматизировать этот issue.

### Окружение

- cw 0.2.0, схема проекта v1 (`status: planning`, черновики в `work/drafts/` с `target: story/chapters/...`).

comments.body: Реализовано в #11: обычная проверка не шумит типографикой рабочих черновиков, доступен явный --draft-typography и команда fix-prose-typography с предпросмотром, применением и откатом.

title: CW-PROSE-103: проз-линт только для результирующих глав; типографские фиксы — автоматические

body:
## Affected component

Creative Writing Skills plugin 0.8.1, bundled `cw` CLI 0.1.0: schema, draft lifecycle, indexes, context selection, migration, and project contract.

## Minimal reproduction

1. Create a canonical schema-v1 project with accepted `story/chapters/chapter-003.md` and `story/chapters/chapter-004.md`.
2. Prepare an accepted bonus episode that belongs between those chapters but is not a numbered main chapter.
3. Try to target `story/side-stories/omake-001.md` from the draft lifecycle.
4. `cw draft accept` rejects the target because it must be `story/chapters/<name>.md`.
5. Put the episode in `story/chapters/` instead. The schema requires a positive integer `number`; reusing a neighboring number makes chapter context ambiguous, while renumbering the main chapters makes their metadata stop matching their displayed chapter numbers.

## Expected behavior

The canonical project should support accepted side stories without classifying them as main chapters. One possible contract:

- a managed `story/side-stories/` directory with its own generated `_index.md`;
- a document kind such as `side-story`, with an optional subtype such as `omake` or `interlude`;
- explicit placement metadata anchored to a durable manuscript document, for example `after: story/chapters/chapter-003.md`;
- support for this target and placement in `draft create`, `draft accept`, migration, structure checks, reindexing, prose checks, and context planning;
- an aggregate reading order that can place the side story between its neighboring chapters without changing the main chapter numbers.

The exact directory and metadata names can follow the repository's conventions; the essential requirement is a durable non-chapter manuscript role with deterministic placement.

## Actual behavior

Schema v1 recognizes manuscript prose only when its direct parent is `story/chapters`. The draft lifecycle validates every accepted target against that directory. Chapter context scans only `story/chapters`, orders documents by unique positive integer `number`, and reports duplicate numbers as unresolved. There is no managed side-story role, generated index, placement anchor, or migration destination.

## Sanitized evidence

Relevant bundled CLI behavior:

- `schema.py`: `parent == "story/chapters"` is the only path mapped to document kind `chapter`;
- `drafts.py`: a draft target outside `story/chapters/<name>.md` raises `draft target must be story/chapters/<name>.md`;
- `context.py`: chapter neighbors are collected only from `story/chapters` and keyed by integer `number`;
- `indexes.py`: only `story/chapters/_index.md` exists for manuscript prose;
- `migration.py`: manuscript destinations are normalized to `story/chapters`.

## Impact

Writers cannot canonically publish omake, interludes, bonus scenes, or other side stories at a defined point in reading order. They must either leave accepted prose under `work/`, misclassify it as a numbered chapter, renumber the main manuscript, or maintain an unsupported local layout that the CLI cannot index, accept, or load as chapter context.

## Environment

- Creative Writing Skills plugin: 0.8.1
- bundled `cw`: 0.1.0
- canonical schema: v1
title: Support accepted side stories with ordered manuscript placement

body:
## Affected component

Bundled `cw` CLI (`project-maintenance` skill, `resources/cli/cw.py`), version cw 0.1.0 — `migrate --preview` / `migrate --apply` plan loading.

## Minimal reproduction

On stock macOS, where `/tmp` is a symlink to `/private/tmp`:

```bash
cd <project>
python3 <plugin>/resources/cli/cw.py migrate --plan --format json > /tmp/plan.json
# edit/resolve the plan, recompute plan-hash, then:
python3 <plugin>/resources/cli/cw.py migrate --preview /tmp/plan.json --expect-plan-hash <hash>
```

The same file content loaded through the real path succeeds:

```bash
python3 <plugin>/resources/cli/cw.py migrate --preview /private/tmp/plan.json --expect-plan-hash <hash>
# -> exit 0, status: preview
```

Direct call of the CLI's own loader shows the difference is purely the path spelling:

```python
load_migration_plan(Path("/private/tmp/plan.json"))  # -> OK, hash, 116 operations
load_migration_plan(Path("/tmp/plan.json"))          # -> MigrationPlanError
```

## Expected behavior

The documented workflow (agent-workflows.md) says: "Run `migrate --plan --format json` from the legacy project and save its output as an agent working file." On macOS, `/tmp` is the conventional location for such a working file, so a plan saved there should either load successfully (e.g., resolve the plan path's symlinked directories before the no-follow directory walk), or the error should be actionable — naming the offending component and the remedy.

## Actual behavior

Exit 1 (conflict) with the message:

```text
migration plan parent has a directory link or non-directory component
```

The message does not identify `/tmp` as the symlinked component, does not mention `/private/tmp`, and gives no recovery hint. The cause is `_open_directory_no_follow()` in `cwcli/migration.py`, which walks every `os.path.abspath()` component of the plan path with `O_NOFOLLOW` and rejects the first symlinked directory component.

## Sanitized evidence

```text
/private/tmp -> OK   (same function, same file)
/tmp         -> MigrationPlanError: migration plan parent has a directory link or non-directory component
```

## Impact

On stock macOS (no unusual local setup), any agent or author that saves the migration plan under `/tmp` — a natural reading of "save its output as an agent working file" — hits an opaque hard failure at the mandatory preview/apply step. Recovery requires knowing the internal no-follow traversal implementation. The same failure class presumably applies to any plan path with a symlinked ancestor directory, not only `/tmp`.

## Environment

- cw 0.1.0, Python 3.12.6
- macOS 26.5 (darwin), where `/tmp` → `/private/tmp` is a stock symlink
title: cw migrate: plan file under /tmp rejected on macOS (/tmp is a symlink to /private/tmp)

## Problem

The successful v0.7.0 Release workflow emitted deprecation warnings because several actions still target the Node.js 20 action runtime. GitHub currently forces them to run on Node.js 24.

Affected workflow: `.github/workflows/release.yml`

Observed actions:

- `actions/checkout@v4`
- `actions/setup-node@v4`
- `softprops/action-gh-release@v2`

Run evidence: https://github.com/InkyQuill/creative-writing-skills/actions/runs/33249420616

## Expected

The release workflow uses action versions that natively support the current GitHub Actions Node runtime and completes without runtime-deprecation annotations.

## Notes

The v0.7.0 release itself succeeded, including validation and publication of all 31 skill archives. This is follow-up maintenance, not a release blocker. Verify upstream action compatibility and changelogs before changing pinned major versions.
title: Update release actions for the Node.js 24 runtime
